identification.summary: TAG-56 is a temporary designator used by Recorded Future's Insikt Group for a suspected Iran-nexus threat activity group. Insikt identified a phishing and credential-theft attack in early November 2022 against the Washington Institute, a US think tank, which it assessed as highly likely led by an Iran-nexus group [S1]. The credential-theft page masqueraded as a Microsoft registration form for the 2022 Sir Bani Yas Forum hosted by the UAE government [S1]. Insikt assessed the activity as likely part of a broader campaign using URL shorteners, a tradecraft it described as common among Iran-nexus groups such as APT42 and Phosphorus [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Early November 2022 (Insikt identification of the Washington Institute phishing activity); report published 2022-11-29 [S1].
identification.notes: TAG-56 is a Recorded Future temporary group name and not a Microsoft name; no Microsoft mapping was found. Malpedia states TAG-56 shares similarities with APT42 [S3]; this does not establish that TAG-56 and APT42 are the same cluster.

attribution.confidence: Recorded Future Insikt Group assessed the attack as highly likely led by an Iran-nexus threat activity group, and describes the group as 'suspected' Iran-nexus in the report title [S1]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Insikt cites tradecraft (URL shorteners, spoofed registration pages) common among Iran-nexus groups such as APT42 and Phosphorus [S1].

objectives: Credential theft from a US think-tank staff member via a spoofed forum registration page [S1]. Broader intent is not stated in the sources reviewed.

targeting.notes: The only confirmed victim is the Washington Institute, a US think tank, in November 2022 [S1]. Insikt assessed the activity as likely part of a wider, ongoing campaign, so other targets are probable but not identified in the sources reviewed [S1].

capabilities.summary: Spearphishing leading to a fake Microsoft-branded registration page for credential theft, with URL shorteners directing victims to the malicious pages [S1]. Malpedia's summary adds fake registration pages and spearphishing delivered through encrypted chat platforms such as WhatsApp or Telegram, and use of shared web hosts and recycled code [S3]. Search-result summaries of the Insikt report indicate hosting on Namecheap shared hosting and reuse of page code, but the full report could not be opened to confirm [S1]. No malware or exploits were reported for this cluster in the sources reviewed.

campaigns.name: Washington Institute credential-theft phishing (Sir Bani Yas Forum lure)
campaigns.summary: Insikt identified phishing and follow-on credential theft against the Washington Institute using a fake Microsoft registration form for the 2022 UAE-hosted Sir Bani Yas Forum. Insikt assessed it as part of a broader campaign using URL shorteners.

campaigns.name: Insikt Group publication
campaigns.summary: Recorded Future published the TAG-56 report.

diamond.adversary: Suspected Iran-nexus threat activity group tracked by Recorded Future as TAG-56, with possible overlap with APT42 [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Spearphishing, spoofed Microsoft registration page, URL shorteners, and reportedly recycled page code [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Credential-theft domains and URL shorteners [S1]. Shared web hosting and recycled code are noted by Malpedia [S3]. Specific domains were not verified from the full report.
diamond.victim: Washington Institute, a US think tank [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Policy-community targeting using a Gulf-state diplomatic forum lure, consistent with Iran-nexus collection against Middle East policy audiences. This is an analytic inference; the sources reviewed do not state intent [S1].
diamond.technology: Microsoft account credentials and email; reliance on user trust in forum registration pages [S1].

gaps: The full Recorded Future report (and its PDF) could not be opened; WebFetch failed for recordedfuture.com, so details came from search-result summaries of it [S1].
Domains, hosting details, and the Insikt recommendations were not verified from the primary text.
No Microsoft actor name or MITRE group ID was found.
Activity after November 2022 attributable to TAG-56 is unknown.
SOCRadar APT42 profile (imported lead) was not reviewed.
The WhatsApp/Telegram delivery detail comes from Malpedia only [S3].
Whether TAG-56 is APT42 or a distinct cluster is unresolved; only Malpedia notes similarities [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: TAG-56 is a threat actor group that shares similarities with the APT42 group. They use tactics such as fake registration pages and spearphishing to target victims, often using encrypted chat platforms like WhatsApp or Telegram. TAG-56 is believed to be part of a broader campaign led by an Iran-nexus threat activity group. They have been observed using shared web hosts and recycled code, indicating a preference for acquiring purpose-built infrastructure rather than establishing their own.
